beats.note: Britannica says the text was thought to be random words until the 1990s.

beats.name: Cicero
beats.role: Britannica dates his ethics treatise De finibus bonorum et malorum to 45 BCE. Wikipedia places the source in sections 1.10.32 and 1.10.33.

beats.note: Open Culture says it is a piece of dolorem, Latin for pain. Wikipedia says the 1914 Loeb edition breaks off at "do-" and resumes with "lorem ipsum" two pages later.

beats.name: Letraset
beats.role: Wikipedia says today's version derives from Letraset transfer sheets first published in 1966. Britannica says Aldus PageMaker added it in the 1980s.

beats.text: A Latin scholar traced it in the 1990s.
beats.note: Britannica credits Richard McClintock with the discovery. Wikipedia says he published the link in a 1994 letter.

beats.text: A Roman essay on pain became the placeholder for every page.
